text:
greg: heads up — after upgrading the kotlin sample to Retrofit3 + coroutines we're seeing requests hang past our coroutine timeout and then trigger duplicate Authenticator refreshes. looks like callTimeout isn't being honored when the coroutine job is cancelled.
maya: can you describe the setup? are you using kotlinx.withTimeout or OkHttp callTimeout?
greg: both. client: `OkHttpClient.Builder().callTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS).authenticator(AppAuthenticator()).build()` Retrofit suspend service used from a coroutine with `withTimeout(8_000) { api.postSomething() }`. When we cancel the coroutine because withTimeout throws, okhttp seems to keep the underlying call alive for another ~10s and when it finally gets a 401 our Authenticator runs and refreshes the token, but the original coroutine has already retried leading to duplicate refresh attempts across concurrent callers.
henry: interesting — coroutine cancellation doesn't automatically cancel the OkHttp call unless you wire it. Retrofit's suspend adapter usually ties cancellation to call.cancel(), but depending on our retrofit/coroutines adapter version that might be flaky with Retrofit3. Which adapter are you using?
greg: using retrofit-kotlinx-coroutines-adapter 1.0.0-beta and our wrapper that calls `suspendCancellableCoroutine` to enqueue the call. It looks like our wrapper is missing the cancel handler on the continuation in edge cases (race between timeout and call completion).
leo: can you paste the enqueue wrapper?
greg: simplified version: ```kotlin
suspend fun <T> Call<T>.awaitResponse(): Response<T> = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  enqueue(object : Callback<T> {
    override fun onResponse(call: Call<T>, response: Response<T>) { cont.resume(response) }
    override fun onFailure(call: Call<T>, t: Throwable) { cont.resumeWithException(t) }
  })
  // missing cont.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() } in some paths due to earlier kotlin stdlib bug we worked around
}
```
maya: yeah that is the root cause — without invokeOnCancellation the coroutine times out but okhttp call continues. add `cont.invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() }` and you should see the underlying call aborted immediately and no duplicate refreshes.
henry: also note that OkHttp's callTimeout cancels on the OkHttp level and will trigger onFailure eventually, but it's slower and doesn't affect the coroutine timeout behavior. We want coroutine cancellation to drive call.cancel() synchronously.
greg: added invokeOnCancellation and repro with stress test (20 concurrent calls) looks clean now. previously we saw Authenticator hit 3x per expired token under heavy load. now it's 1x.
tara: can we add a small test in the sample app that asserts cancellation cancels the OkHttp call? a MockWebServer that stalls and a withTimeout wrapper should validate. Also add a snippet in the README showing the correct suspend wrapper pattern.
leo: created ticket INF-4700 for "Kotlin suspend wrapper missing cancellation hook -> OkHttp calls survive coroutine timeout -> duplicate token refreshes" and linked the sample PR.
ci-bot: INF-4700 created and assigned area/devex priority/medium.
maya: one more thought: also document that using OkHttp's async call API plus `call.timeout()` (per-call timeout) is another safety net but not a substitute for proper coroutine cancellation wiring.
henry: agreed. I'll add a short blurb in the SDK auth guide about cancellation semantics: 1) always `invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() }` in suspend wrappers, 2) prefer `.header(...)` vs `addHeader` for redirect-sensitive headers (see earlier threads), 3) test with MockWebServer under concurrency.
greg: thanks — i'll open the PR with test + fix and reference INF-4700. ping me for review. :thumbsup:
